operations.description: Ignore .claude/worktrees/: the worktree manager creates them there, and a linked worktree is a full second copy of the tree, so the residue scanner counted every duplicated hook as a new violation whenever any session had one open.

edits.find:
# Worktree-per-agent runtime state: linked worktrees + the manager's registry
# (machine-local paths; never shipped — install.sh copies .claude/ wholesale)
.worktrees/
.claude/state/
edits.replace:
# Worktree-per-agent runtime state: linked worktrees + the manager's registry
# (machine-local paths; never shipped — install.sh copies .claude/ wholesale)
.worktrees/
# .claude/worktrees/ is where the manager actually creates them, and it was NOT
# covered here. A linked worktree is a full second copy of the tree, so the
# silent-failure residue scanner walked into it and counted every duplicated hook
# as a new violation -- reddening the gate for every session whenever ANY session
# had a worktree open. Runtime state, never source.
.claude/worktrees/
.claude/state/

operations.description: Ship the same ignore downstream: installed projects run the same worktree manager and the same gate.
